He moves between writing code, crafting technical essays, and experimenting with tactile digital interfaces.

- **Clarity over complexity**: Preferring simple, maintainable architectures over unnecessary abstraction layers.
- **Details matter**: Obsessing over typography, keyboard accessibility, micro-interactions, and visual contrast.

## 2. Engineering Projects & Full Case Studies

### Project 1: Lumina Engine
- **Category**: Developer Tool / Local-First Systems
- **Status**: Prototype (2026)
- **Tech Stack**: Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, WebAssembly (Wasm/Rust), IndexedDB
- **Live URL**: https://ranaaryan.online/work/lumina-notes
- **GitHub Repository**: https://github.com/ranaaryandev/lumina-engine

**Problem Statement**:
Traditional web note-taking apps rely heavily on remote cloud databases, resulting in typing latency, cloud lock-in, and degraded performance when notes exceed thousands of files.

**Technical Approach**:
Built a local-first browser client that stores data directly in IndexedDB and offloads query parsing and text indexing to a Rust-compiled WebAssembly module running inside a background Web Worker.

**Architecture**:
- React UI layer with zero heavy state synchronization overhead
- Web Worker running a compiled Wasm fuzzy search engine
- IndexedDB storage layer wrapped in a lightweight transactional schema
- Virtual list renderer handling 10,000+ notes at 60 FPS

**Development Process & Chronology**:
- *Initial Approach*: Experimented with client-side FlexSearch and Fuse.js running directly on the main UI thread. Indexing 5,000+ notes caused visible typing lag and dropped frames.
- *Architectural Pivot*: Shifted text tokenization and fuzzy matching logic into a compiled Rust WebAssembly module, running asynchronously inside a dedicated Web Worker thread.
- *Key Breakthrough*: Implemented shared memory ArrayBuffer transfer across Worker postMessage boundaries, eliminating serialization overhead and locking query response times under 5ms.

**Result**:
Achieved sub-5ms query response times over 10,000 markdown documents completely client-side without a single server round-trip.

---

### Project 2: Tactile Specs
- **Category**: UI & Accessibility Inspector
- **Status**: Open Source / Independent Experiment (2025)
- **Tech Stack**: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Chrome API, Radix Primitives
- **Live URL**: https://ranaaryan.online/work/craft-ui-spec
- **GitHub Repository**: https://github.com/ranaaryandev/tactile-specs

**Problem Statement**:
Accessibility auditing tools are often buried inside heavy developer suite dashboards or produce overwhelming PDF dumps that developers ignore during daily UI development.

**Technical Approach**:
Created an inline design overlay that highlights low-contrast elements and small touch targets directly on the DOM canvas with live WCAG math calculations.

**Development Process & Chronology**:
- *Initial Approach*: First built as a standard React overlay component injected into the page DOM tree. This resulted in CSS style bleed from host website stylesheets corrupting the inspector UI.
- *Architectural Pivot*: Re-architected the inspector widget inside an isolated Shadow DOM container with closed encapsulation, isolating extension CSS styles completely.
- *Key Breakthrough*: Created a custom tree-walking algorithm that resolves computed alpha channel composition across stacked DOM layers to accurately compute real contrast ratios.

**Result**:
Audits live DOM pages in real-time under 16ms per frame, making accessibility checks smooth during component development.

---

### Project 3: Pulse Privacy
- **Category**: Full-Stack Telemetry Engine
- **Status**: Concept Project (2025)
- **Tech Stack**: Next.js App Router, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Tailwind CSS, Recharts
- **Live URL**: https://ranaaryan.online/work/pulse-analytics
- **GitHub Repository**: https://github.com/ranaaryandev/pulse-privacy

**Problem Statement**:
Traditional web analytics platforms harvest intrusive personal data, require annoying cookie consent banners, and slow down site load speeds with massive tracker scripts.

**Technical Approach**:
Designed a cookieless telemetry architecture that generates daily rotating salt hashes to track unique sessions without storing IP addresses or tracking cookies.

**Development Process & Chronology**:
- *Initial Approach*: Attempted client-side local storage session tokens. This failed privacy principles because local storage tokens persist across visits and mimic tracking cookies.
- *Architectural Pivot*: Designed a server-side daily rotating salt hash (`SHA-256(IP + UserAgent + DailySalt)`), destroying raw IP logs immediately after generating anonymous session IDs.
- *Key Breakthrough*: Automated in-memory Redis hyperloglog counters for unique visitor counts, achieving 99% session accuracy with zero persistent disk logging of user identifiers.

**Result**:
Prototyped a clean dashboard engine that provides direct traffic metrics with zero cookie notices and sub-1KB tracking script overhead.

---

### Project 4: Papyrus CLI
- **Category**: CLI & Tooling
- **Status**: Live Utility (2025)
- **Tech Stack**: TypeScript, Node.js, Ink, Cheerio, Commander
- **Live URL**: https://ranaaryan.online/work/paper-cli
- **GitHub Repository**: https://github.com/ranaaryandev/papyrus-cli

**Problem Statement**:
Reading documentation and tech articles often involves dealing with popups, auto-playing video ads, and bloated navigation headers that break focus.

**Technical Approach**:
Built a CLI binary that fetches web pages, parses raw HTML content, strips unnecessary layout noise, and renders formatted markdown directly into your terminal.

**Development Process & Chronology**:
- *Initial Approach*: Initially relied on simple regex HTML stripping. This broke code block formatting, merged text paragraphs together, and stripped essential technical code snippets.
- *Architectural Pivot*: Adopted a structural AST pipeline using Cheerio DOM parsing combined with Turndown markdown conversion, preserving clean hierarchy and code blocks.
- *Key Breakthrough*: Implemented Ink React components to render ANSI terminal text with responsive terminal window width wrapping and dark mode syntax highlighting.

**Result**:
Delivers instant distraction-free terminal reading in under 200ms per article fetch.
